# What Groq API keys the library redacts, and what it leaves alone.
#
# Every key here is built from the ordered run
# 0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz, which no real credential is. That run is
# thirty-six characters, so a body carries it and fourteen characters more — the
# shortest body the pattern reads, since the count is a floor. It is spelled in
# lowercase where the case does not matter and in uppercase where the case is
# what a case is about: base62 holds the letters of both, so either spelling is
# a body.

patterns: groq-api-key

# The one prefix Groq has issued an API key with. There is a single kind of
# string here rather than a table of them: one key serves every model Groq
# serves and every endpoint it is served at, so nothing in the value says what
# it may be spent on, and the cases below are that one shape in the places a key
# is written.

case:     a key in an environment assignment
in:       GROQ_API_KEY=gsk_0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456789abcd
out:      GROQ_API_KEY=«groq-api-key»

case:     a key in the bearer authorization header Groq's endpoints are called with
in:       Authorization: Bearer gsk_0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456789abcd
out:      Authorization: Bearer «groq-api-key»

case:     a key in json
in:       {"apiKey":"gsk_0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456789abcd"}
out:      {"apiKey":"«groq-api-key»"}

case:     a key on a command line
in:       curl -H "Authorization: Bearer gsk_0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456789abcd" https://api.groq.com/openai/v1/chat/completions
out:      curl -H "Authorization: Bearer «groq-api-key»" https://api.groq.com/openai/v1/chat/completions

case:     a key in a configuration environment block
in:       "env": {"GROQ_API_KEY": "gsk_0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456789abcd"}
out:      "env": {"GROQ_API_KEY": "«groq-api-key»"}

# The alphabet the fifty characters are written in. It is base62 — the letters
# of both cases and the digits — which is what all four rulesets stating a shape
# admit behind the prefix. The two characters base64url adds, the hyphen and the
# underscore, are not admitted, and either of them ends a body.

case:     a body written in capitals
in:       gsk_0123456789ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ0123456789ABCD
out:      «groq-api-key»

case:     a body carrying a hyphen
in:       gsk_0123456789abcdefghij-lmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456789abcd
out:      gsk_0123456789abcdefghij-lmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456789abcd

case:     a body carrying an underscore
in:       gsk_0123456789abcdefghij_lmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456789abcd
out:      gsk_0123456789abcdefghij_lmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456789abcd

# The lengths either side of fifty. Groq states no length for a key, and no
# alphabet and no checksum either; three rulesets read fifty-two characters and
# the fourth reads fifty to fifty-four, and every key any of them publishes is
# fifty-two. The count is read as a floor rather than exactly, and at the
# shortest of those: forty-nine characters are not a key, and fifty-one are one
# key to the end of its run rather than a key and a character left over. What
# the floor costs is the middle case below — a key cut short of fifty keeps
# every random character written in front of the cut, and none of them is
# redacted.

case:     a body of fifty characters is a key
in:       gsk_0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456789abcd
out:      «groq-api-key»

case:     a body of forty-nine characters is not
in:       gsk_0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456789abc
out:      gsk_0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456789abc

case:     an alphabet run longer than the floor is a key to the end of it
in:       gsk_0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456789abcde
out:      «groq-api-key»

# The eight characters every published key carries at the twenty-first
# character of its body. Two of the four carry WGdyb3FY, which is the base64
# encoding of the vendor's own name with a byte of the value either side of it,
# and the two noseyparker publishes carry the same eight with the q written
# over. The pattern reads none of that: no Groq page and no published rule
# states the marker, and a marker read wrong locates nothing at all. So the two
# cases below are one key each, and what tells them from text is the prefix, the
# alphabet and the floor.

case:     a key carrying the marker the published keys carry
in:       gsk_0123456789abcdefghijWGdyb3FYklmnopqrstuvwxyz012345
out:      «groq-api-key»

case:     a key of the same shape carrying no marker
in:       gsk_0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456789abcd
out:      «groq-api-key»

# What a key may be written against. There is no boundary on either side of the
# prefix, so a key keeps its span whatever word character it abuts — and where
# the run of its alphabet carries on past the floor, what carries it on is
# redacted with the key. A hyphen and an underscore end the run instead.

case:     a key after an underscore
in:       GROQ_API_KEY_gsk_0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456789abcd
out:      GROQ_API_KEY_«groq-api-key»

case:     a key after a letter
in:       xgsk_0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456789abcd
out:      x«groq-api-key»

case:     a word written against a key
in:       gsk_0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456789abcdsuffix
out:      «groq-api-key»

case:     a hyphenated word written against a key
in:       gsk_0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456789abcd-suffix
out:      «groq-api-key»-suffix

case:     an underscored word written against a key
in:       gsk_0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456789abcd_suffix
out:      «groq-api-key»_suffix

case:     a key at the end of a sentence
in:       the key is gsk_0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456789abcd.
out:      the key is «groq-api-key».

# Two keys written together. The three letters the prefix opens with belong to
# the alphabet a body is written in, so a body may close with gsk and the
# underscore of the next key stand directly behind it; the second key begins
# three characters before the first one ends, the two spans overlap and are
# redacted as one. Written with nothing at all between them the first body
# reaches three characters into the second prefix and stops at the underscore
# behind them, so those two overlap as well. Written with a space between them
# the two are separate values, and both go.

case:     a key beginning inside the key before it
in:       gsk_0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456789agsk_0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456789abcd
out:      «groq-api-key»

case:     two keys with nothing between them
in:       gsk_0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456789abcdgsk_0123456789ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ0123456789ABCD
out:      «groq-api-key»

case:     two keys separated by a space
in:       gsk_0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456789abcd gsk_0123456789ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ0123456789ABCD
out:      «groq-api-key» «groq-api-key»

# A snake_case name whose segment closes on the three letters the prefix opens
# with carries a whole prefix — and where fifty unbroken characters of the
# alphabet stand behind it, everything from the gsk onward is redacted and only
# the syllable in front of it stays. The tightening that would rule that out is
# the demand that no letter and no digit stand in front of a prefix; it is
# declined, because the key written inside another has the last letter of a body
# in front of its own prefix and the demand would leave that key in the text
# with its body whole. What holds the ordinary name away instead is the floor,
# which the next underscore of such a name ends long before.

case:     a name closing on the prefix with a body behind it
in:       debugsk_0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456789abcd
out:      debu«groq-api-key»

case:     a name closing on the prefix with a short segment behind it
in:       debugsk_level=1 debugsk_host=localhost
out:      debugsk_level=1 debugsk_host=localhost

# What this pattern redacts that nobody issued. The prefix closes with an
# underscore, which standard base64 writes nowhere, so only a base64url encoding
# can hold one — and where fifty base62 characters follow, the run from the
# prefix to the end of them is redacted whether or not Groq issued it. That is
# the answer rather than a fault in it, because such a run is a key's format
# exactly and nothing in the text tells the two apart: sparing these would spare
# a real key written the same way. What is taken is a stretch of a value that
# was already opaque to a reader.

case:     the prefix inside a longer run of base64url
in:       payload=zzzzgsk_0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456789abcdzzzz
out:      payload=zzzz«groq-api-key»

case:     the prefix where a signature stands
in:       eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiJ9.eyJzdWIiOiJhYmMifQ.zzzzgsk_0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456789abcdzzzz
out:      eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiJ9.eyJzdWIiOiJhYmMifQ.zzzz«groq-api-key»

# A digest written behind the prefix, which is the one over-match here that
# takes a value a reader had a use for. Hexadecimal digits are base62 and a
# digest carries nothing that ends a run, so gsk_ and the sixty-four characters
# of a SHA-256 are a key's format exactly, and both are redacted. Declining them
# would mean declining every key Groq happened to write in the digits alone,
# which is a whole credential against a cache key. What holds either side of it
# is the floor and the prefix: a SHA-1 is forty characters, ten short of a body,
# an MD5 is thirty-two, and a hyphen is no character the prefix carries.

case:     a sha256 behind the prefix
in:       gsk_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef
out:      «groq-api-key»

case:     a sha256 in a cache key
in:       key: gsk_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef
out:      key: «groq-api-key»

case:     a sha1 behind the prefix, ten characters short of a body
in:       gsk_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01234567
out:      gsk_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01234567

case:     an md5 behind the prefix
in:       gsk_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef
out:      gsk_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef

case:     a sha256 behind a hyphen rather than the prefix
in:       gsk-0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef
out:      gsk-0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef

# And what this pattern leaves alone. The first three are the prefix, read in
# the case Groq writes it, in the underscore it closes with and in that
# underscore being there at all. The two after them are the alphabet and the
# anchor: a body a space has broken, and a run of the right length with no
# prefix in front of it. The last two hold no underscore where the prefix wants
# one, so neither holds a position to be found at however long it runs.

case:     an uppercase prefix
in:       GSK_0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456789abcd
out:      GSK_0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456789abcd

case:     a hyphen where the prefix carries an underscore
in:       gsk-0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456789abcd
out:      gsk-0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456789abcd

case:     the prefix without its closing underscore
in:       gsk0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456789abcd
out:      gsk0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456789abcd

case:     a body broken by a space
in:       gsk_0123456789abcdefghij lmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456789abcd
out:      gsk_0123456789abcdefghij lmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456789abcd

case:     a run of the right length opening with no prefix
in:       0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456789abcd
out:      0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456789abcd

case:     a hexadecimal digest
in:       sha1=0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01234567
out:      sha1=0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01234567

case:     prose
in:       there is no credential in this sentence
out:      there is no credential in this sentence
